description_full: TRX Gold Corporation engages in the exploration, development, and production of mineral property in Tanzania. Its flagship project is the Buckreef Gold Project in Tanzania. The company was formerly known as Tanzanian Gold Corporation and changed its name to TRX Gold Corporation in May 2022. The company was incorporated in 1990 and is based in Oakville, Canada.
ceo_bio: Mr. Stephen  Mullowney B.B.A., C.A., C.F.A., CPA | CEO & Director | Age 48 | Compensation: $953,937 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 336 people. Revenue per employee of $171K ranks in the bottom quartile among Basic Materials peers, with revenue growing 23%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $10K of free cash flow annually. CEO compensation is 6× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: TRX Gold Corporation is a micro-cap basic materials business with a $288M market cap on $58M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -3.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 8% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 44%.

The business throws off $3M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.48× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
